paragraphs.title: Vows of valuation before the Lord

easy.question: To whom did the Lord speak at the beginning of the passage?
answers: Moses
Aaron
The Israelites
easy.explanation: The first verse says, “The Lord spake unto Moses.”

easy.question: To whom was Moses told to speak?
answers: The priests
The Israelites
The king of Israel
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Speak unto the children of Israel.”

easy.question: What does the person described in the verse do?
answers: Offers a sacrifice
Goes to war
Makes a vow to the Lord
easy.explanation: The verse describes someone who makes a special vow concerning a person’s valuation before the Lord.

medium.question: What is the order in which the message is delivered?
answers: The Israelites speak to Moses, and Moses to the Lord
The Lord speaks to Moses, and Moses instructs the Israelites
Moses speaks to the Israelites, and they command the Lord
medium.explanation: The Lord first speaks to Moses, who is then told to speak to the Israelites.

medium.question: In the phrase “make a singular vow,” what is a vow?
answers: A promise or commitment to the Lord
A question directed to the Lord
A song of thanksgiving to the Lord
medium.explanation: A vow is a solemn promise or commitment, here made in relation to the Lord.

medium.question: According to the verse, what does the vow concern?
answers: Building an altar
Dividing the land
The valuation of persons before the Lord
medium.explanation: The verse says the persons shall be for the Lord by the stated valuation.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the command being given to Moses but intended for the Israelites?
answers: The message was given to a leader to pass on to the people
The command was only for Moses
The Israelites were unrelated to the command
challenge.explanation: The passage presents Moses as the mediator who conveys the Lord’s words to the Israelites.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “when a man” emphasize at the beginning of the command?
answers: Only priests may make vows
The command concerns an Israelite who makes a vow
Only national leaders may value persons
challenge.explanation: The wording describes an ordinary person performing the action, without identifying him as a priest or leader.

challenge.question: Which phrase shows that the vow is directed to the Lord rather than being merely a private agreement?
answers: “Moses”
“The children of Israel”
“For the Lord”
challenge.explanation: The phrase “for the Lord” explicitly connects the vow and valuation with the Lord.

questions.question: What can we infer from the command being given to Moses but intended for the Israelites?
answers: The message was given to a leader to pass on to the people
The command was only for Moses
The Israelites were unrelated to the command
questions.explanation: Moses serves as the mediator who conveys the Lord’s words to the Israelites.

questions.question: What does the phrase “when a man” emphasize at the beginning of the command?
answers: Only priests may make vows
The command concerns an Israelite who makes a vow
Only national leaders may value persons
questions.explanation: The wording describes an ordinary person performing the action.

questions.question: Which phrase shows that the vow is directed to the Lord rather than being merely a private agreement?
answers: “Moses”
“The children of Israel”
“For the Lord”
questions.explanation: “For the Lord” explicitly connects the vow with the Lord.

easy.question: What valuation is set for a male from twenty through sixty years old?
answers: Fifty shekels
Thirty shekels
Twenty shekels
easy.explanation: A male aged twenty through sixty is valued at fifty shekels.

easy.question: What valuation is set for a female from twenty through sixty years old?
answers: Fifty shekels
Thirty shekels
Ten shekels
easy.explanation: A female in that age range is valued at thirty shekels.

easy.question: What valuation is set for a male from five through twenty years old?
answers: Ten shekels
Five shekels
Twenty shekels
easy.explanation: A male aged five through twenty is valued at twenty shekels.

medium.question: What is the difference between the valuation of a male and a female aged five through twenty?
answers: Five shekels
Ten shekels
Fifteen shekels
medium.explanation: The male is valued at twenty shekels and the female at ten, a difference of ten.

medium.question: In “thy estimation,” what does “estimation” mean?
answers: Your age
Your sex
The monetary value assigned to you
medium.explanation: The passage gives a monetary amount for each person’s valuation.

medium.question: Which age group appears after the group aged five through twenty?
answers: Those aged sixty and above
Those aged one month through five
Those aged twenty through sixty
medium.explanation: The next group listed is people aged sixty and above.

challenge.question: Which group is assigned the lowest valuation?
answers: A female aged one month through five
A male aged sixty and above
A female aged five through twenty
challenge.explanation: A female aged one month through five is valued at three shekels, the lowest amount listed.

challenge.question: For which age group is a male assigned the highest valuation?
answers: One month through five
Twenty through sixty
Sixty and above
challenge.explanation: A male aged twenty through sixty is valued at fifty shekels, the highest amount.

challenge.question: How many shekels higher is the valuation of a male aged sixty and above than that of a female aged five through twenty?
answers: Ten shekels
Three shekels
Five shekels
challenge.explanation: The male is valued at fifteen shekels and the female at ten, a difference of five.

questions.question: Which group is assigned the lowest valuation?
answers: A female aged one month through five
A male aged sixty and above
A female aged five through twenty
questions.explanation: A female aged one month through five is valued at three shekels, the lowest amount listed.

questions.question: For which age group is a male assigned the highest valuation?
answers: One month through five
Twenty through sixty
Sixty and above
questions.explanation: A male aged twenty through sixty is valued at fifty shekels.

questions.question: How many shekels higher is the valuation of a male aged sixty and above than that of a female aged five through twenty?
answers: Ten shekels
Three shekels
Five shekels
questions.explanation: Fifteen minus ten equals five shekels.

paragraphs.title: Valuing someone who cannot afford the standard amount

easy.question: Who values the person when he is poor?
answers: The priest
The king
The judge
easy.explanation: The verse says, “the priest shall value him.”

easy.question: Before whom is the person brought?
answers: The Levites
The priest
The elders
easy.explanation: He is to present himself before the priest.

easy.question: According to what does the priest set the valuation?
answers: The person’s age
His place of residence
His ability to pay
easy.explanation: The priest values him according to the ability of the one who made the vow.

medium.question: What is the order described in the verse?
answers: The person appears before the priest, and then the priest values him
The priest values him, and then he is brought to the priest
The person pays, and then the priest chooses the value
medium.explanation: First he appears before the priest; afterward the priest values him.

medium.question: In this context, what does “poorer than thy estimation” mean?
answers: Strong and healthy
Young in age
Poor or lacking means
medium.explanation: The phrase describes someone unable to afford the standard valuation.

medium.question: Why does the priest value the person differently?
answers: Because the person is poor and cannot meet the standard amount
Because he forgot his vow
Because the priest does not know the law
medium.explanation: The valuation is adjusted to the person’s ability to pay.

challenge.question: What social principle emerges from the verse?
answers: Everyone must pay the same amount regardless of circumstances
The obligation is adjusted to a person’s financial ability
Only wealthy people may make vows
challenge.explanation: The priest values the person according to what the one who vowed can afford.

challenge.question: What is the priest’s special role in this case?
answers: To release the person from every obligation
To collect the payment himself
To set a suitable valuation according to the person’s ability
challenge.explanation: The priest determines a valuation appropriate to the person’s means.

challenge.question: What does “according to his ability that vowed” mean?
answers: What the person is able to pay
What he can lift with his hand
What he found along the way
challenge.explanation: The phrase refers figuratively to the person’s financial ability.

questions.question: What social principle emerges from the verse?
answers: Everyone must pay the same amount regardless of circumstances
The obligation is adjusted to a person’s financial ability
Only wealthy people may make vows
questions.explanation: The valuation is based on what the person can afford.

questions.question: What is the priest’s special role in this case?
answers: To release the person from every obligation
To collect the payment himself
To set a suitable valuation according to the person’s ability
questions.explanation: The priest determines a valuation appropriate to the person’s means.

questions.question: What does “according to his ability that vowed” mean?
answers: What the person is able to pay
What he can lift with his hand
What he found along the way
questions.explanation: It refers to the amount the person can obtain and pay.

easy.question: Which animal becomes holy when given to the Lord?
answers: An animal suitable for sacrifice
Any unclean animal
Only a wounded animal
easy.explanation: An animal suitable for an offering to the Lord shall be holy.

easy.question: What may not be done to an animal dedicated to the Lord?
answers: Present it before the priest
Exchange it for another animal
Have its value assessed
easy.explanation: The passage forbids changing or exchanging the dedicated animal.

easy.question: What is done with an unclean animal that is not suitable for sacrifice?
answers: It is burned
It is immediately given to the priest
It is presented before the priest
easy.explanation: The unclean animal is to be presented before the priest.

medium.question: What happens if someone exchanges a dedicated animal for another animal?
answers: Only the new animal becomes holy
Both animals become holy
Both animals become common
medium.explanation: The original animal and the animal given in exchange are both holy.

medium.question: In “if he will at all redeem it,” what does “redeem” mean?
answers: Sell it to someone else
Buy it back
Offer it immediately
medium.explanation: Redemption means taking it back by paying its assessed value plus a fifth.

medium.question: What is the proper order concerning a dedicated unclean animal?
answers: It is exchanged and then valued by the priest
It is sacrificed and then a fifth is added
It is presented before the priest, who values it
medium.explanation: The animal is first brought to the priest, who then determines its value.

challenge.question: What is the main difference between an animal suitable for sacrifice and an unclean animal in this passage?
answers: The suitable animal becomes holy, while the unclean animal is valued by the priest
The suitable animal is sold, while the unclean animal is sacrificed
There is no legal difference
challenge.explanation: The suitable animal is treated chiefly as holy; the unclean animal is assessed by the priest.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the prohibition against exchanging a good animal for a bad one, or a bad one for a good one?
answers: Only unclean animals may be exchanged
The dedication remains binding even after an attempted exchange
The good animal loses its holiness
challenge.explanation: Both the original and the exchanged animal become holy.

challenge.question: What does adding “a fifth part” mean when redeeming the animal?
answers: Adding one-fifth to the assessed value
Paying only one-fifth of the value
Paying five times the value
challenge.explanation: A fifth is added to the value set by the priest.

questions.question: What is the main difference between an animal suitable for sacrifice and an unclean animal in this passage?
answers: The suitable animal becomes holy, while the unclean animal is valued by the priest
The suitable animal is sold, while the unclean animal is sacrificed
There is no legal difference
questions.explanation: The suitable animal becomes holy, whereas the unclean animal is assessed.

questions.question: What can we infer from the prohibition against exchanging a good animal for a bad one, or a bad one for a good one?
answers: Only unclean animals may be exchanged
The dedication remains binding even after an attempted exchange
The good animal loses its holiness
questions.explanation: Both the original and the exchanged animal become holy.

questions.question: What does adding “a fifth part” mean when redeeming the animal?
answers: Adding one-fifth to the assessed value
Paying only one-fifth of the value
Paying five times the value
questions.explanation: The redeemer adds one-fifth to the value set by the priest.

paragraphs.title: Dedicating a house to the Lord

easy.question: Who values the house dedicated to the Lord?
answers: The priest
The person who dedicated it
The neighbor
easy.explanation: The priest is the one who estimates the house.

easy.question: To whom does the man dedicate his house?
answers: The king
The Lord
His family
easy.explanation: The house is dedicated as holy to the Lord.

easy.question: What must be added if the person redeems his house?
answers: A tenth of the money
Half the money
A fifth of the money
easy.explanation: He must add a fifth to the assessed value.

medium.question: What happens after the priest values the house?
answers: The priest’s valuation stands
The house is destroyed
The person receives another house
medium.explanation: The house stands according to the priest’s valuation.

medium.question: In “if he that sanctified it will redeem his house,” what does “redeem” mean?
answers: Sell his house
Buy back his house
Move into his house
medium.explanation: He takes the house back by paying its value plus a fifth.

medium.question: Why must the person add money when redeeming his house?
answers: He must add a fifth to the assessed value
The priest changes the house’s value
The house has become larger
medium.explanation: The law requires an additional fifth of the assessed value.

challenge.question: What does “whether it be good or bad” teach about valuing the house?
answers: Only a good house is valued
The priest values it regardless of its condition
The person who dedicated it chooses the value
challenge.explanation: The priest values the house whether its condition is good or bad.

challenge.question: What is the proper order of the actions in these verses?
answers: The house is redeemed, then dedicated, then valued
The house is valued, and then it may be redeemed with an added fifth
A fifth is added, and then the priest dedicates the house
challenge.explanation: The house is first dedicated and valued; afterward it may be redeemed.

challenge.question: To whom does the house belong after it is redeemed and the extra payment is made?
answers: The person who dedicated it
The priest
All Israel together
challenge.explanation: The house becomes his again after redemption and payment.

questions.question: What does “whether it be good or bad” teach about valuing the house?
answers: Only a good house is valued
The priest values it regardless of its condition
The person who dedicated it chooses the value
questions.explanation: The priest values the house whether its condition is good or bad.

questions.question: What is the proper order of the actions in these verses?
answers: The house is redeemed, then dedicated, then valued
The house is valued, and then it may be redeemed with an added fifth
A fifth is added, and then the priest dedicates the house
questions.explanation: The house is first valued and may then be redeemed with a fifth added.

questions.question: To whom does the house belong after it is redeemed and the extra payment is made?
answers: The person who dedicated it
The priest
All Israel together
questions.explanation: The house returns to the person who dedicated it.

paragraphs.title: Dedicating an inherited field and the Year of Jubilee

easy.question: What kind of field is described in verses 16–21?
answers: A field of one’s possession
A field belonging to the temple
A foreigner’s field
easy.explanation: The passage refers to a field of a person’s possession.

easy.question: What valuation is given for an homer of barley seed?
answers: Ten shekels
Fifty shekels
One hundred shekels
easy.explanation: An homer of barley seed is valued at fifty shekels.

easy.question: Who calculates the value of a field dedicated after the Jubilee?
answers: The king
The owner alone
The priest
easy.explanation: The priest calculates the amount according to the years remaining until the Jubilee.

medium.question: What happens if a person dedicates his field in the year of Jubilee?
answers: The stated valuation remains in force
The field immediately becomes the priest’s property
The field has no value
medium.explanation: If dedicated in the Jubilee year, the field stands according to the stated valuation.

medium.question: In “it shall be abated from thy estimation,” what does “abated” mean?
answers: Added to the value
Subtracted from the value
Given to the priest
medium.explanation: The value is reduced when fewer years remain until the Jubilee.

medium.question: What must the person add if he redeems the field?
answers: A tenth of the amount
Half the amount
A fifth of the amount
medium.explanation: He must add a fifth of the assessed value when redeeming the field.

challenge.question: Why is a field dedicated after the Jubilee valued according to the years remaining until the Jubilee?
answers: Fewer remaining years mean a shorter period of use
The field becomes smaller after the Jubilee
The priest may change the land’s price at will
challenge.explanation: The passage links the value to the remaining years, so a shorter period lowers the value.

challenge.question: What happens if the person does not redeem the field but sells it to another man?
answers: It immediately returns to him
It shall not be redeemed any more
It is sold again every year
challenge.explanation: The verse says that it shall not be redeemed any more.

challenge.question: What happens to the field when it goes out in the Jubilee in this case?
answers: It returns to the family
It becomes an ordinary field
It becomes holy and belongs to the priest
challenge.explanation: It becomes holy to the Lord, and its possession belongs to the priest.

questions.question: Why is a field dedicated after the Jubilee valued according to the years remaining until the Jubilee?
answers: Fewer remaining years mean a shorter period of use
The field becomes smaller after the Jubilee
The priest may change the land’s price at will
questions.explanation: The value is tied to the number of years remaining until the Jubilee.

questions.question: What happens if the person does not redeem the field but sells it to another man?
answers: It immediately returns to him
It shall not be redeemed any more
It is sold again every year
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly says it shall not be redeemed any more.

questions.question: What happens to the field when it goes out in the Jubilee in this case?
answers: It returns to the family
It becomes an ordinary field
It becomes holy and belongs to the priest
questions.explanation: The field becomes holy to the Lord, and its possession belongs to the priest.

paragraphs.title: A purchased field and the standard shekel

easy.question: What is done with a purchased field that a person dedicates to the Lord?
answers: The priest calculates its value
The field is destroyed
The field is given to the king
easy.explanation: The priest calculates its value up to the year of Jubilee.

easy.question: When does the field return to its original owner?
answers: At New Year
In the year of Jubilee
After seven days
easy.explanation: The field returns in the year of Jubilee.

easy.question: How many gerahs are in a sanctuary shekel?
answers: Ten gerahs
Fifteen gerahs
Twenty gerahs
easy.explanation: The verse states that twenty gerahs make a shekel.

medium.question: Why does the priest calculate the field’s value up to the year of Jubilee?
answers: Because the field is always given as a gift
Because the field returns to its owner in the Jubilee
Because the field is sold to the priest in the Jubilee
medium.explanation: The calculation concerns the period until the field returns in the Jubilee.

medium.question: What does “a field which he hath bought” mean in this passage?
answers: A field received as an inheritance
An abandoned field
A field that was purchased
medium.explanation: The verse distinguishes a purchased field from an inherited possession.

medium.question: What happens to the payment made when the value is calculated?
answers: It is holy to the Lord
It is returned to the person
It is given only to the field’s former owner
medium.explanation: The payment is given as a holy thing unto the Lord.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the field returning in the Jubilee to the person who sold it?
answers: The sale was permanent
The field could not be cultivated
The transfer was temporary
challenge.explanation: Its return shows that the transfer did not permanently cancel the family’s ownership rights.

challenge.question: What distinguishes this field from an ordinary inherited field?
answers: It was purchased rather than inherited
It could not be planted
It was outside the land
challenge.explanation: The passage specifically calls it a field that was bought.

challenge.question: What is the practical meaning of defining a shekel as twenty gerahs?
answers: Every field is worth twenty gerahs
A fixed weight unit is established for calculating value
Payment must be made only in groups of twenty coins
challenge.explanation: The verse establishes a standard unit for measuring and calculating payment.

easy.question: Which animals are mentioned as having firstborn that belong to the Lord?
answers: An ox or a sheep
A goat or a camel
A horse or a donkey
easy.explanation: The verse says, “whether it be ox, or sheep: it is the Lord’s.”

easy.question: To whom does the firstborn of a clean animal belong?
answers: The owner alone
The Lord
The priest alone
easy.explanation: The firstborn already belongs to the Lord.

easy.question: What must be added when an unclean animal is redeemed?
answers: A tenth of its value
Half its value
A fifth of its value
easy.explanation: The person must add a fifth to its assessed value.

medium.question: What happens to an unclean animal if it is not redeemed?
answers: It is sold according to its value
It always remains with its owner
It is immediately given to the priest
medium.explanation: If it is not redeemed, it is sold according to the valuation.

medium.question: In “if it be not redeemed,” what does “redeemed” mean?
answers: Given as a gift
Bought back or released by payment
Slaughtered immediately
medium.explanation: The context contrasts redemption with sale, so it means being bought back.

medium.question: Why can a person not dedicate the firstborn of a clean animal himself?
answers: Because it belongs to no one
Because animals may not be used
Because it already belongs to the Lord
medium.explanation: The firstborn is already the Lord’s and cannot be dedicated again.

challenge.question: What is the main difference between the firstborn of a clean animal and an unclean animal?
answers: The clean animal’s firstborn already belongs to the Lord, while the unclean animal may be redeemed by value
The unclean animal is holier than the clean firstborn
Only the clean firstborn is sold by value
challenge.explanation: The clean animal’s firstborn belongs to the Lord from the outset; an unclean animal may be redeemed or sold.

challenge.question: What does the repeated phrase “according to thy estimation” indicate?
answers: The price depends only on the animal’s age
The animal is valued according to an assigned assessment
The owner may choose any price
challenge.explanation: It emphasizes that redemption or sale follows an established valuation.

challenge.question: What does “Only” at the beginning of the verse emphasize?
answers: All animals must be sold
Only unclean animals belong to the Lord
There is an exception: a firstborn already belonging to the Lord cannot be dedicated again
challenge.explanation: The word introduces an exception to the general rule about dedicating animals.

paragraphs.title: Things wholly devoted to the Lord

easy.question: What may not be done to a thing devoted to the Lord?
answers: It may not be sold or redeemed
It may not be kept at home
It may not be brought to the sanctuary
easy.explanation: The passage says it shall not be sold or redeemed.

easy.question: Which things are mentioned as being capable of being devoted to the Lord?
answers: Silver, gold, and clothing
A person, an animal, and a field
A house, vineyard, and tool
easy.explanation: The passage mentions a person, an animal, and a field of one’s possession.

easy.question: What is a devoted thing called in the passage?
answers: An ordinary gift
A minor holy thing
Most holy
easy.explanation: Every devoted thing is described as most holy to the Lord.

medium.question: Why cannot a devoted thing be sold or redeemed?
answers: Because it is wholly dedicated to the Lord
Because it belongs only to the family
Because fields may never be sold
medium.explanation: It is most holy to the Lord and therefore cannot be sold or redeemed.

medium.question: In this context, what is a “devoted thing”?
answers: Something lent to others
Something dedicated and removed from ordinary use
Something lost and never found
medium.explanation: The context describes something devoted completely to the Lord.

medium.question: What is the order of ideas in these verses?
answers: A punishment is described, followed by the sale of a field
Animal redemption is described, followed by the dedication of a person
Devotion is described generally, followed by devotion of a person
medium.explanation: The first verse treats devoted things generally; the next gives a special rule for a person devoted to the Lord.

challenge.question: What is the main difference between the devoted thing in verse 28 and a person devoted in verse 29?
answers: Verse 29 explicitly says the person cannot be redeemed and shall be put to death
Verse 28 permits sale, while verse 29 forbids it
In verse 29 the person can redeem himself
challenge.explanation: Verse 29 adds the special rule that the person cannot be redeemed but shall surely be put to death.

challenge.question: What does the repeated word “every” suggest in these verses?
answers: The law applies only to fields
The rule has broad application to all the devoted things described
The verses concern only one person
challenge.explanation: The wording indicates that the rule is not limited to a single case.

challenge.question: What wording distinguishes verse 28 from verse 29?
answers: Verse 28 mentions the Lord, but verse 29 does not
Verse 28 speaks of sale and redemption, while verse 29 speaks of redemption and death
Verse 28 speaks only of a person, while verse 29 speaks only of an animal
challenge.explanation: Verse 28 prohibits selling or redeeming; verse 29 says the devoted person cannot be redeemed and shall die.

paragraphs.title: The tithe of the land belongs to the Lord

easy.question: What does the verse discuss?
answers: The tithe of the land
Building the tabernacle
Sabbath laws
easy.explanation: The verse concerns the tithe of the land.

easy.question: To whom does the tithe belong?
answers: The king
The Lord
The priest alone
easy.explanation: The verse says, “it is the Lord’s.”

easy.question: How is the tithe described?
answers: Pure
New
Holy
easy.explanation: The tithe is holy to the Lord.

medium.question: Which two kinds of produce are mentioned as part of the tithe?
answers: Animals and fish
Seed of the land and fruit of the tree
Bread and wine
medium.explanation: The verse mentions the seed of the land and the fruit of the tree.

medium.question: What does “tithe” mean in “all the tithe of the land”?
answers: A tenth part
The first harvest
A special gift
medium.explanation: A tithe is one part out of ten of the produce.

medium.question: What follows from calling the tithe “holy unto the Lord”?
answers: It has a special status and is dedicated to the Lord
It may be used for any purpose
It belongs only to the landowner
medium.explanation: The phrase shows that the tithe is dedicated to the Lord rather than being ordinary property.

challenge.question: What important detail might be missed in the verse?
answers: The tithe comes only from tree fruit
The tithe includes both seed and fruit
The tithe comes only from animals
challenge.explanation: The verse names two sources: the seed of the land and the fruit of the tree.

challenge.question: What is emphasized by the repeated words “the Lord’s” and “holy unto the Lord”?
answers: The tithe belongs only to the land
The tithe is given only once
The tithe belongs to the Lord and is dedicated to him
challenge.explanation: The wording emphasizes both the Lord’s ownership and the tithe’s holiness.

challenge.question: What kind of produce is discussed in the verse?
answers: Agricultural produce from the land and trees
Only money collected from the people
Only temple vessels
challenge.explanation: The seed of the land and fruit of the tree are agricultural produce.

easy.question: What must a person add when redeeming his tithe?
answers: A fifth
Half
A tenth
easy.explanation: The verse says he shall add a fifth part.

easy.question: Who is described as redeeming the tithe?
answers: The priest
A man
The king
easy.explanation: The verse begins, “if a man will at all redeem.”

easy.question: What does the person redeem?
answers: His house
His field
His tithe
easy.explanation: The verse refers to redeeming part of his tithes.

medium.question: What is the order of actions described in the verse?
answers: The man redeems his tithe and then adds a fifth
He adds a fifth and then gives his tithe
He receives a tithe and then redeems the priest
medium.explanation: He first redeems the tithe and then adds a fifth to it.

medium.question: In “if a man will at all redeem,” what does “redeem” mean?
answers: Keep
Buy back or release by payment
Distribute
medium.explanation: It refers to taking the tithe back by making the required payment.

medium.question: When must a fifth be added according to the verse?
answers: When a person receives another’s tithe
When a person gives away all his property
When a person redeems his tithe
medium.explanation: The fifth is required when a person redeems his own tithe.

challenge.question: What does “he shall add thereto” show about the fifth?
answers: It is added to the basic amount
It replaces the tithe
It is given only after a year
challenge.explanation: The wording shows that the fifth is an addition to the tithe’s value.

challenge.question: What can we infer from “if” at the beginning of the verse?
answers: Everyone must always redeem his tithe
The extra payment applies when a person chooses to redeem the tithe
Only the priest may redeem the tithe
challenge.explanation: “If” introduces a conditional case: when a person redeems the tithe, he adds a fifth.

challenge.question: If the tithe is worth 100, and the fifth is one-fifth of its value, how much is paid altogether?
challenge.explanation: One-fifth of 100 is 20, so the total is 120.

paragraphs.title: The tithe of the herd and flock

easy.question: What happens to every tenth animal of the herd and flock?
answers: It becomes holy to the Lord
It is sold in the market
It is given to the shepherd
easy.explanation: The tenth animal shall be holy to the Lord.

easy.question: What passes under the rod as the animals are counted?
answers: Only the tenth animal
All the herd and flock
Only the best animals
easy.explanation: The animals pass under the rod so they can be counted.

easy.question: What may not be done to the tenth animal?
answers: Count it
Dedicate it
Exchange it for another animal
easy.explanation: The verse says it shall not be changed or exchanged.

medium.question: How is the animal that becomes holy determined?
answers: By its size
By the order of counting, as the tenth animal
By the owner’s choice
medium.explanation: It becomes holy because it is tenth in the count.

medium.question: In “it shall not be redeemed,” what does “redeemed” mean?
answers: Bought back or released from its dedication
Counted again
Kept until the following year
medium.explanation: The verse teaches that the tithe animal cannot be bought back or released from its dedication.

medium.question: What happens if a person nevertheless exchanges the tenth animal?
answers: Only the new animal becomes holy
Both become common
Both the original and the exchanged animal become holy
medium.explanation: The verse makes both animals holy in the event of an exchange.

challenge.question: What does “he shall not search whether it be good or bad” mean?
answers: The tenth animal is not chosen by quality
Only a good animal may be chosen
Every animal must be inspected by the priest
challenge.explanation: The tenth is determined by counting, not by whether the animal is good or bad.

challenge.question: Why does exchanging the animal not help someone avoid dedicating it?
answers: Animals may not be counted more than once
Both the original and the exchanged animal become holy
The exchanged animal immediately returns to the flock
challenge.explanation: The law prevents cancellation by making both animals holy.

challenge.question: What conclusion follows from “the tenth shall be holy” and “he shall not search whether it be good or bad”?
answers: Only an excellent animal may be tithed
The owner may postpone dedicating the tenth
The tithe’s holiness depends on its number, not its quality
challenge.explanation: The animal becomes holy because it is tenth, regardless of its quality.

paragraphs.title: Conclusion of the commandments in Leviticus

easy.question: Who commanded these commandments?
answers: The Lord
Moses
The Israelites
easy.explanation: The verse says, “which the Lord commanded Moses.”

easy.question: To whom did Moses deliver the commandments?
answers: The Egyptians
The Israelites
The kings of the nations
easy.explanation: They were given to Moses for the children of Israel.

easy.question: Where were the commandments given?
answers: Jerusalem
Egypt
Mount Sinai
easy.explanation: The verse says they were given on Mount Sinai.

medium.question: What is the order in which the commandments were delivered?
answers: The Lord commanded Moses, and Moses delivered them to Israel
Israel commanded Moses, and Moses commanded the Lord
Moses commanded the Lord, and the Lord delivered them to Israel
medium.explanation: The Lord is the commander, Moses receives the commandments, and Israel is the intended audience.

medium.question: What does “in mount Sinai” indicate?
answers: The city of Sinai
Mount Sinai
The land of Egypt
medium.explanation: The wording identifies the place as Mount Sinai.

medium.question: What relationship between Moses and Israel is shown by the verse?
answers: Moses received the command and conveyed it to Israel
Moses was one of Israel’s kings
Moses received the commandments only for himself
medium.explanation: Moses received the Lord’s commandments and passed them on to the Israelites.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the wording “which the Lord commanded Moses for the children of Israel”?
answers: The commandments were created by Israel
Moses had no role in delivering them
The commandments came from the Lord and were conveyed through Moses to Israel
challenge.explanation: The wording presents the Lord as the source, Moses as the mediator, and Israel as the audience.

challenge.question: Why is this verse suitable at the end of Leviticus?
answers: It summarizes that the commandments in the book were given by the Lord
It describes the beginning of Moses’ reign
It describes the Exodus from Egypt
challenge.explanation: The verse summarizes the commandments and emphasizes their divine source.

challenge.question: What is the significance of mentioning Mount Sinai at the end?
answers: The commandments were only for Mount Sinai’s residents
The commandments are connected with the setting in which the divine instruction was given
Moses built Mount Sinai
challenge.explanation: Mount Sinai identifies the sacred place associated with the giving of the commandments.

questions.question: What can we infer from the wording “which the Lord commanded Moses for the children of Israel”?
answers: The commandments were created by Israel
Moses had no role in delivering them
The commandments came from the Lord and were conveyed through Moses to Israel
questions.explanation: The Lord is the source, Moses is the mediator, and Israel is the audience.

questions.question: Why is this verse suitable at the end of Leviticus?
answers: It summarizes that the commandments in the book were given by the Lord
It describes the beginning of Moses’ reign
It describes the Exodus from Egypt
questions.explanation: It summarizes the commandments discussed and emphasizes their divine source.

questions.question: What is the significance of mentioning Mount Sinai at the end?
answers: The commandments were only for Mount Sinai’s residents
The commandments are connected with the setting in which the divine instruction was given
Moses built Mount Sinai
questions.explanation: Mount Sinai is associated with the giving of the divine commandments.
